oewn-00613356-v.learner: to use your memory, or to have the power to use it.
examples: As she grew older, she found it harder to remember.

oewn-00613035-v.learner: to call someone or something back to mind and keep their memory alive, for example in a ceremony.
examples: Every November the town gathers to remember those who died in the war.

oewn-00884044-v.learner: to mention someone to another person as a way of sending greetings or showing friendship.
examples: Please remember me to your parents when you see them.

oewn-00884323-v.learner: to mention someone in a kind and favourable way, for example in a prayer.
examples: She promised to remember him in her prayers.

oewn-02361566-v.learner: to show someone that you value them and are thankful to them.
examples: He remembered the old gardener with a gift of money in his will.

oewn-01241629-n.learner: the act of taking part in what a group is doing.
examples: The teacher was pleased by the students' engagement in the group project.

oewn-01220349-n.learner: the act of giving someone a job.
examples: The engagement of a new cook was left to the housekeeper.

oewn-00271763-n.learner: a job for a performer or a group of performers that lasts only for a limited time.
examples: The band has a two-week engagement at a theatre in the city.

oewn-07352714-n.learner: the way two parts touch each other by fitting together.
examples: The engagement of the two gears makes both wheels turn together.

oewn-00959711-v.learner: to say something again, or to copy what someone says.
examples: The parrot repeated every word the children said.
He failed the course and had to repeat it the next year.

oewn-01731369-v.learner: to bring back a theme that came earlier in the same piece of work.
examples: The last movement repeats the theme heard at the very start of the symphony.
He threw the ball high into the air.

oewn-11451868-n.learner: a light wind, usually one that feels fresh.
examples: A cool air came off the river in the evening.

oewn-08516085-n.learner: all the air that surrounds the Earth.
examples: Smoke from the cities spreads through the air around the whole Earth.

oewn-06265931-n.learner: the means through which radio and television programmes are sent out.
examples: The show goes on the air at nine o'clock.

oewn-00301267-n.learner: travel in an aircraft, such as a plane.
examples: We decided to go by air rather than by train.

oewn-14866873-n.learner: one of the four elements that people once believed, following Empedocles, made up the universe, and which was linked with blood as one of the body's humours.
examples: Early thinkers held that everything was made of earth, water, fire and air.

oewn-10183826-n.learner: the person in charge of a school.
examples: He was made master of the grammar school when he was only thirty.

oewn-10318314-n.learner: a person who directs the work of other people.
examples: The farm workers asked their master which field to plough first.

connotation.why: casts those directed as servants rather than employees

oewn-10772598-n.learner: a fighter who is able to beat their rivals.
examples: After years of winning, the old champion had at last met his master.

oewn-10318465-n.learner: a person who holds a master's degree from a university or other place of higher learning.
examples: After two more years of study she became a master of science.

oewn-10318579-n.learner: an officer who has a licence to command a ship used for trade.
examples: The master of the cargo ship ordered the crew to lower the boats.

oewn-03902681-n.learner: a key that lets you get in everywhere.
examples: The caretaker used the master to open the locked office.

oewn-03732765-n.learner: an original, such as a sound recording, from which copies can be made.
examples: The studio kept the master safe and sent out only copies.

oewn-13313810-n.learner: something given to make up for a wrong that was done.
examples: He demanded satisfaction for the insult to his family.

oewn-13371012-n.learner: the paying of a debt, or the carrying out of something you are bound to do.
examples: The court recorded the full satisfaction of the debt.

oewn-14111894-n.learner: a sudden, short loss or weakening of awareness that the person does not remember afterwards, sometimes with slight twitching or fluttering eyelids, and common in petit mal epilepsy.
examples: During an absence the child stared blankly for a few seconds and her eyelids fluttered.

oewn-00104546-r.learner: further on in time, or in order, or in degree.
examples: The talks have moved forward a great deal since the spring.

oewn-00277124-r.learner: at or toward the front of a ship, or the cockpit of a plane.
examples: The cargo was stored forward, close to the bow.

oewn-05150324-n.learner: a reason for wanting something to be done.
examples: The road was closed in the interest of safety.

oewn-13307824-n.learner: a right to something or a legal share in it, or a money stake in something.
examples: She sold her interest in the family business.

oewn-00432492-n.learner: an activity that fills your time and thoughts, usually in a pleasant way.
examples: Gardening became her main interest after she stopped working.

oewn-07984994-n.learner: a group of people who control some area of activity and share the same aims, usually spoken of in the plural.
examples: The big oil interests fought hard against the new tax.

oewn-01159815-v.learner: to use up supplies or materials.
examples: This old heater uses far too much electricity.

oewn-02606487-v.learner: to try to get, or to get, what you want by taking advantage of someone or something.
examples: He only used her to get close to her rich father.

connotation.why: implies selfish exploitation of a person

oewn-01167359-v.learner: to take or consume something regularly or out of habit.
examples: She does not use drugs of any kind.

connotation.why: suggests a drug habit rather than plain taking
